And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#2064. Scott Parker’s Promotion Blueprint Offers West Ham A Way Forward

With Scott Parker set to become West Ham United’s new head coach, I’ve been looking back at his three Championship promotion campaigns to get a better idea of what supporters can expect. Rather than simply guessing how he’ll set up the Hammers, I wanted to examine the formations and players he actually used at Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham.

And having looked through the evidence, I’m increasingly convinced that Parker will favour a 4-2-3-1 at West Ham. It was his preferred system during Burnley’s remarkable 2024/25 promotion campaign, and he also used it at both Bournemouth and Fulham, although he was prepared to switch formations when necessary.

As discussed earlier today, his record of securing promotion with three different clubs was always likely to appeal to West Ham’s decision-makers. But it’s the way he achieved those promotions that interests me, particularly given the problems we’ve witnessed under Nuno Espírito Santo.

Parker’s record is impressive enough without dressing it up. He took Fulham up through the play-offs in 2020, secured automatic promotion with Bournemouth in 2022 and then guided Burnley back to the Premier League with 100 points in 2025.

What I found particularly interesting was that all three sides used a 4-2-3-1 in their final promotion-season matches. That doesn’t mean Parker played the formation every week, but it does provide a useful starting point when trying to establish his tactical preferences.

Those figures show the goals conceded across each 46-match league campaign, rather than just the final matches. And the progression is interesting, with Parker’s most recent promotion-winning team producing by far his strongest defensive record.

However, there’s an important distinction between his Bournemouth and Burnley sides. According to the Premier League’s tactical analysis, Bournemouth actually used 4-3-3 on 27 occasions during their promotion campaign, compared with 13 starts in 4-2-3-1. Parker increasingly favoured the latter towards the end of the season.

Burnley, on the other hand, were much more closely associated with 4-2-3-1. The Premier League’s examination of their promotion campaign identified it as Parker’s first-choice formation, with two midfielders providing defensive protection and the number ten contributing heavily to the press.

To give you lovely C&H readers a clearer picture, I’ve taken the starting elevens from Fulham’s 2020 play-off final victory against Brentford and Burnley’s final Championship fixture against Millwall in 2025.

Both were recorded as 4-2-3-1, although the responsibilities of individual players were not identical.

The obvious similarity is the presence of two central midfielders behind three more advanced players. That’s the aspect of the formation I find particularly appealing for West Ham.

I’ve already seen plenty of people complaining about Parker’s supposedly negative football, but I find that criticism slightly strange when you look at what he achieved at Burnley.

Sixteen goals conceded in 46 Championship games is incredible. Make no mistake about it. His team also recorded 30 clean sheets, a remarkable achievement which helped Burnley finish the season with 100 points.

Burnley scored 69 goals that season, compared with Leeds United’s 95. So there is a legitimate discussion to be had about whether Parker’s football can sometimes be too cautious, but I certainly wouldn’t dismiss the defensive record as a negative.

In fact, I would expect the first priority of any manager arriving at West Ham to be fixing the defence. It’s crap.

There’s a certain irony here, of course. West Ham had the most porous defence in the Premier League when Nuno Espírito Santo arrived last season, and we all remember how Graham Potter’s team seemingly couldn’t defend a corner. Improving that situation was supposed to be one of Nuno’s principal jobs.

Yet in the end, we were left with a pragmatic defensive manager who had seemingly forgotten how to park the bus.

As Nuno’s dismissal following the defeat against West Bromwich Albion demonstrated, the club eventually ran out of patience with performances that were neither defensively convincing nor particularly effective going forward.

I think Parker’s defensive organisation is precisely what West Ham should be looking for now. And if that improved structure can give our more creative players a little extra freedom, then so much the better.

Nuno was brought in to fix Potters awful defence

Looking at Parker’s previous teams, I believe 4-2-3-1 would be a sensible fit for the players he is inheriting at West Ham. The formation provides two central midfielders who can protect the defence, which should immediately help address the problems we’ve had with opponents dominating the middle of the pitch.

But the benefit isn’t purely defensive. Having that protection behind the attacking players should allow them to operate with considerably more freedom, rather than constantly worrying about what happens when possession is lost.

It also provides something I believe West Ham have desperately needed: a proper number ten.

And I don’t mean somebody like Mohamedou Kanté being shoehorned into a false-nine position he’s not equipped for. I mean a genuine playmaker with an eye for a pass, a stepover and a trick, somebody capable of unlocking a defence rather than simply occupying a position on the pitch.

That’s where Divine Mukasa comes into it for me, although I could also see Manor Solomon operating in that role.

I think either could benefit from having two midfielders behind them, particularly if Jarrod Bowen is given the freedom to get into more dangerous attacking positions.

Of course, there’s an important qualification here. Parker’s Burnley number ten was often expected to work extremely hard without the ball, pressing opponents and helping protect the midfield. So it would be wrong to assume he will automatically select a traditional playmaker simply because he uses 4-2-3-1.

Nevertheless, the formation offers that possibility, and I think it’s one West Ham’s attacking players would hopefully enjoy playing in.

There’s another reason I’m reluctant to accept the suggestion that Parker can only produce negative football.

His Bournemouth team were particularly effective at pressing opponents during their promotion season. The Premier League’s tactical analysis recorded them as the Championship’s most intense pressing side by passes per defensive action, with opponents averaging just 10.8 passes before Bournemouth intervened defensively.

That suggests a manager who is capable of setting up a team to win the ball back aggressively, rather than simply sitting deep and hoping to nick a goal.

Bournemouth also conceded only 39 league goals during that campaign, demonstrating that Parker was able to combine a relatively aggressive approach without sacrificing defensive organisation.

And that’s really what I’d like to see at West Ham.

I’m not expecting Parker to turn us into some sort of attacking footballing circus, nor do I think fans should judge him on whether every game produces three or four goals.

But I do expect a team that knows its jobs, defends properly, competes from the first whistle and provides enough attacking support for its better players to make a difference.

The evidence from his previous promotion campaigns suggests Parker is capable of delivering that sort of structure. Whether he can reproduce it at West Ham remains to be seen, but there are genuine reasons for optimism.

Three promotions with three different clubs, a remarkable defensive record at Burnley and a clear history of using systems that could suit West Ham’s attacking players.

For me, that’s a far more useful way of assessing Scott Parker than simply dismissing him as a negative manager before he’s even started.

#2063. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners target Brazilian teenager Eduardo Pape

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are increasing their interest in Cruzeiro youngster Eduardo Pape.

Despite the fact he has yet to play for the senior side in Brazil, the 17-year-old has attracted interest from a number of clubs. It is understood that Arsenal is keeping an eye on the youngster. Newcastle United and Bayern Munich are also linked with the midfielder.

The move could be a good fit with the Gunners liking to identify young talent early on. However, Pape is still very much in the early stages of his career, and any move would be seen as an investment into his future.

Arsenal are reportedly targeting Pape as a potential signing in 2027. The teenager is valued at around £33m.

Pape has already had previous experience playing for Cruzeiro’s Under-20s. He’s played 32 times and scored three goals and three assists.

He has left a successful headline in junior football as well. Pape has netted six goals in eight matches and strives for a place in the Brazilian U17 World Cup squad.

The tournament gives an opportunity to demonstrate his skills. The scouts will closely monitor the tournament, so any team interested in the player will be able to see his progress.

Of course, not just Arsenal would want to sign him. Clubs like Newcastle and Bayern Munich have already expressed interest in securing him. This is likely to cause a competitive atmosphere.

There is a concern that there hasn’t been any senior-level play from Pape. As he has never played first-team football before. It will be difficult to see how he will adapt to playing in Europe.

The contract is until December 2029, meaning Cruzeiro are in a strong position. There isn’t a huge need for the Brazilian club to rush into any decisions, meaning Pape can get some experience in a comfortable environment before moving abroad.

However, they have been very successful in the past at bringing in young Brazilian players. Gabriel Martinelli was brought in from Ituano as a teenager and has become an important first team player.

It gives us an insight into what Pape could hope to achieve.

It shows that Arsenal are looking further ahead with their recruitment. Whether they make a move for him remains to be seen. Pape will be one to keep an eye on as we approach the 2027 transfer window.

#2062. I said the priority should have been to sit Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes down…

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Back on 17 August 2026, six days before the 2026-27 Premier League season kicked off, I put an article (‘The priority should have been to sit Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes down’) up on The Mag.

I detailed how Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes were the key figures of the past five years. The manager and (eventual) captain leading Newcastle United to what had felt unimagined riches in the decade and a half before the October 2021 takeover.

Eddie Howe at the top of the tree managing his squad, with Bruno Guimaraes the talisman delivering on and off the pitch.

The second half of the 2021-22 Premier League season saw only Liverpool and Manchester City pick up more points than Newcastle United, incredible stuff by Eddie Howe and whilst Bruno Guimaraes was given time by the manager to settle in, once he scored that stunning backheel winner in his first ever start (at Southampton), Bruno never looked back.

The rest as they say is history. The four full seasons saw Bruno Guimaraes and Eddie Howe lead Newcastle United to three top seven finishes, two cup finals, two Champions League qualifications, two top five finishes, a trophy.

The 2025/26 season was a tough one, reaching the last 16 of the Champions League, the semi-finals of the Carabao, fifth round of the FA Cup, but also finishing 12th in the Premier League. Bruno Guimaraes also suffered his first injury of any magnitude when at NUFC, missing a key couple of months from February into April. I think 58 matches for such a small squad and so few real quality players was a real killer, it was mission impossible in reality in my eyes.

Back on 17 August 2026 I stated: ‘If Newcastle United fans thought that the final stages of the 2025-26 season were disappointing, fair to say that what has followed is far worse. For me it is anyway. This summer was always going to be a tough one, especially due to the UEFA SCR impact that very much limited the financial flex Newcastle United would have. Careful management of transfers in and out as well as the wage bill. The 2026-27 season was for sure going to be seriously challenging come what may.’

Now it is two and a half months after I wrote that and fair to say this season is now looking VERY seriously challenging.

Six days before this season starting, I said that because of all those challenges that our club faced, it was: ‘Something that for me meant the huge priority, the absolute priority, should have been for those in charge at Newcastle United, owners and senior staff, to sit both Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes down together and ask them what it would take for both of them to be totally committed and confident of tackling the 2026/27 season together. Our leaders staying and leading the way. That clearly didn’t happen.’

Back on 17 August 2026 I stated the obvious, well what to me felt obvious anyway: ‘I think that quite clearly Ross Wilson had been given far more power. Not a case of Eddie Howe losing all control but clearly a major shift in how the transfer window would be conducted. My belief is that Eddie Howe ended up with far less say when it came to whether players were sold and at the same time less say on which signings should be made. I think he would have still been able to say no to a signing and not have any forced on him, but Ross Wilson becoming the main man running the recruitment show.’

Back on 17 August 2026 I said my belief on what happened behind the scenes was as follows: ‘I think Kieran Trippier leaving was the first big blow. My belief is that Eddie Howe would certainly have been in favour of trying to keep him for at least one more season but the change in how things were done, meant that in my opinion, the club wouldn’t have offered Trippier the same wages and no surprise he walked away for first team football and a two year contract at Wolves. Anthony Gordon was clearly put up for sale long before last season ended and who knows what Eddie Howe thought about that. I think maybe he was accepting that one of his key players had to be sold to satisfy the UEFA SCR situation. The end of May and the end of the season, Bruno Guimaraes heads off to link up with Brazil whilst Eddie Howe takes a well deserved break. Only a couple of weeks later though and the Sandro Tonali to Tottenham claims began.’

Back on 17 August 2026 my view was: ‘I think now that when this all started in mid-June the writing was on the wall for the Newcastle United manager and captain. I believe that with Eddie Howe still in charge and Bruno and Tonali in tandem in the midfield, Newcastle United could have successfully negotiated the 2026-27 season. What exactly would have counted as success is another thing…but to me it would have been relative success that could have been achieved and that now looks a very tough ask with how things have ended up. With the Trippier and Gordon dominoes having already toppled, once Tonali followed…I think Bruno Guimaraes and Eddie Howe were all but guaranteed to fall as well.’

I went on to say in that piece six days before the NUFC 2026-27 kicking off: ‘I don’t think there is anything wrong with the targeting of young promising players as a key part of the Newcastle United plan, indeed that is what Eddie Howe proved so brilliant at, when recruiting the likes of Hall, Isak, Bruno, Gordon, Livramento, Tonali…However, this summer has seen the recruitment even younger than most of those successes under Howe and far greater risks with far less experience behind them, far more likely to fail and far more likely to take longer to reach their full potential. Newcastle United have shifted to a model that sees the Sporting Director far more pivotal in directing the transfer strategy and just maybe it might prove successful against the odds. However, I do think that for especially this coming season it has put Newcastle United at great risk.’

I take no pleasure in saying it but ‘great risk’ is very much how this now feels for Newcastle United.

I understand people debating whether or not Matthias Jaissle is the right man for Newcastle United but what is without doubt, he was handed a very difficult situation, some would say near impossible. That is, impossible to achieve in the short to medium term anything approaching what Eddie Howe did.

Back on 17 August 2026 I stated (and still believe): ‘If there had been a big sit down with Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes in May, maybe things would have been different, maybe nothing would have been different. At the same time though I think without the pair of them being at the heart of the plan going forward, it massively helped ensure they would both leave. Eddie Howe came back in early July ahead of pre-season and informed the club he would be leaving, volunteering to hold the fort until a replacement was ready to come in. Which turned out to be Matthias Jaissle.’

Speaking of things I still believe to be true.

On 17 August 2026 I said: ‘I don’t buy into this attempt to make out Bruno Guimaraes to be the big bad guy of this summer. I still don’t know what he has done wrong apart from inform the club he wanted to leave? Everything else is smoke and mirrors with talk of a super agent brought in to help get a move and so on. By the same token the Newcastle United hierarchy were clearly quite happy to move out Trippier, Gordon and Tonali for financial reasons, so Bruno Guimaraes can hardly be blamed in my opinion, when he chooses to follow them out as well. The idea that the NUFC owners and senior staff thought that moving these key players out would then still see both Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes up for staying, is straining credibility. The Newcastle United owners believing that, is on a par with when we had the farce of Alexander Isak going on strike throughout summer 2025 and the NUFC owners doing nothing to sort it. Then believing they could turn up at the very end of the window, go round his house and suddenly convince him to change his mind!!’

My article on 17 August 2026 ended with: ‘I hope for the best this coming season but fear the worst. If the worst does happen, I certainly won’t be pointing the finger at Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes if it all goes pear-shaped. The Newcastle United owners have to step up belatedly and produce a cohesive long-term strategy to properly progress the club. If they don’t do that, we will have a lot more to worry about than what happens this coming season.’

Writing this now on 4 November 2026, not a great deal has changed for me.

I am still not pointing the finger of blame at Eddie Howe or Bruno Guimaraes.

My opinion is that the Newcastle United owners wrecked summer 2025 after Eddie Howe had just delivered the most successful NUFC season in living memory for most of us. A huge dereliction of duty in having no actively working Sporting Director or CEO in place, leaving Eddie Howe totally unsupported and no senior staff in place to help ensure the key Howe transfer targets were delivered. The NUFC owners insisting they wouldn’t sell Alexander Isak and then at the very last minute doing a u-turn and the rushed end of window recruitment of Woltemade and Wissa (rather than the likes of Joao Pedro and Hugo Ekitike who Howe had wanted) made what turned out to be a 58 game 2025-26 season with such a small squad an impossible job for Eddie Howe, rather than just very difficult.

Whether it was intentional or not, the shift by the Newcastle United owners in making Ross Wilson the main man then directly led to Eddie Howe leaving. Also ensuring that Bruno Guimaraes was going to be leaving as well.

What happens next at our football club remains to be seen.

As always with Newcastle United I am hoping for the best but fearing the worst.

#2061. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners explore loan move for Real Madrid striker Endrick

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are keeping their options open regarding a January move for Real Madrid striker Endrick, as Mikel Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

The Gunners have been in contact about a loan move for the Brazilian. There is also talk of a permanent move. However, Real Madrid are reluctant to let him leave and feel he has a big future ahead at the club.

Endrick has struggled to earn consistent game time at the Bernabeu.

While he is only 20 years old and has plenty of time left to make his mark at the top level, a new transfer away from Madrid could give him a more consistent role.

Arsenal are among the clubs keeping an eye on Endrick ahead of the January transfer window, reports TEAMtalk.

The forward was loaned to Lyon for the second half of last season to get more regular game time.

However, his representatives are said to be open to looking for another move if things do not improve in Madrid.

It seems Arsenal are interested in signing Endrick on loan with a view to making the move permanent. This will give them time to see how he settles into the Premier League.

However, Real Madrid may be in a strong position. They are still loyal to the young player and would prefer to keep him at the Spanish club.

Arsenal will rely on Madrid being more willing to let him go.

The reported interest from Arsenal comes as Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

Endrick would provide variety to an attacking line-up which has been under pressure of late. His age and potential make a loan deal with an option to make the move permanent an attractive option.

There is also positivity from his previous stint with Lyon. He has already been on a loan move from Madrid and has demonstrated that he can make progress when getting regular game time.

Arsenal have previously signed young talents from Real Madrid.

Martin Odegaard came to north London as a young player after failing to make an impact in the first team at Madrid. He then became a key player for Arteta, taking on the role of captain.

Endrick will be hoping to follow a similar trajectory.

There is no suggestion that any deal is near despite Arsenal’s interest.

Endrick remains an important part of Real Madrid’s long-term plans. His representatives are thought to be looking at other options to help his career develop.

This loan deal would provide a solution for all parties. Arsenal would have another attacker to bring in, Endrick would play more regularly and Madrid would still have an interest in his future.

It will also depend on how willing the Spanish giants are to move their stance before January.

For now, Arsenal are in contact with Endrick as they consider a move. The Brazilian’s future may soon become a topic of interest ahead of the winter transfer window.

#2060. West Ham’s big guns come out with verdict over Scott Parker appointment

Whilst officially West Ham United head into the midweek fixture against Cardiff City without a head coach, the Irons will mix the talents of established coaching duo Gerard Prenderville and Steve Potts with the expertise of sporting director Mark Noble to provide the off-field leadership for tonight’s attempt to arrest their two-game losing run and put some points on the board.

It will be intriguing to see the immediate impact which the sacking of Nuno Epirito Santo has on the Hammers’ dressing room when the whistle blows tonight.

Hopefully that means the end of ‘outcast’ squad members and that players will get utilised within their established positions soon enough, so that the era of square pegs being pushed into round holes is finally ended.

Many will feel relieved that the days of the division of the Hammers’ squad are ended: Now perhaps the handbrake could come off for the careers of several ‘outcasts’.

Behind the scenes the appointment of Scott Parker does seem nailed on, whilst no official pronouncement has yet been made. All roads point to the former Hammer of the Year taking control of the West Ham squad, which is an appointment that has already been welcomed by former players – one a former assistant to David Moyes who is, of course, still pretty close to the club.

Kevin Nolan, former captain during West Ham’s last promotion winning campaign, pronounced judgement on TalkSPORT:

“I’m delighted with the talk that it’s Scotty going in, giving a young British manager an opportunity at a big club. He’s got a track record. It’s going to be a tough season”

Former Irons’ striker turned TV pundit Dean Ashton was similarly positive. Speaking on talksport, Ashton pointed out that West Ham supporters hadn’t had a manager who felt connected with them for many years, but all that would change if and when Parker is confirmed:

“They want to be inspired again. It is important to connect again with the supporters… He’s certainly got fire in his belly and will relish the opportunity to manage West Ham.”

Whilst some fans profess disappointment over the ‘low ambition’ shown by the football club in considering Scott Parker, I’d suggest they’ve picked exactly the right man to do the job.

Forget the long term. Climb the greasy pole out of this hugely challenging division at all costs and back in the Premier League first. Then worry about what kind of football you want to play.

Because failure carries unthinkable financial repercussions for this football club. Right now, I’d suspect on track records alone, there’s nobody better qualified than former West Ham captain Scott Parker to do the job required.

#2059. West Ham official statement names former Newcastle United star as their new manager

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

West Ham have named former Newcastle United and England star Scott Parker as their new manager.

An official announcement on Wednesday morning.

This follows Tuesday’s sacking of Nuno Espírito Santo.

Nuno was sacked with West Ham sitting eighth in the Championship, six points behind league leaders Middlesbrough and the Hammers only two points off third.

Scott Parker taking over ahead of an away game at Cardiff City tonight.

West Ham decided not to renew David Moyes’ contract after the Hammers ‘only’ finished ninth in the 2023-24 Premier League season. They played three consecutive years of European football, two campaigns in the Europe League and winning the Conference League.

Since forcing David Moyes out just over two years ago, West Ham have appointed Julen Lopetegui, Graham Potter, Nuno and now Scott Parker.

The official club statement beginning: ‘West Ham United can confirm that Scott Parker has agreed a deal to become the Club’s new men’s first-team Head Coach. The former Hammers captain, 46, has signed a two-and-a-half year contract at London Stadium, and will take charge of the team for Wednesday evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City. Parker will be assisted by first-team coaches Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, while Mark Noble will also be working closely with his former team-mate. Further details on the permanent structure of Parker’s backroom staff will be announced in due course.’

Scott Parker: “It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a Club that means so much to me and my family. A lot of very fond memories of my time here – four years of probably the best football I played in my career. There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly. More than anything, this is an opportunity that I am very excited about. I feel privileged and honoured to be the guy that wants to lead us back to the Premier League and be the Head Coach of this Football Club at this moment in time. My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion – it’s absolutely running through and that’s the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That’s exactly why I’m here and why I want to be here. From my first calls with Karim [Virani] and Daniel [Křetínský], it was clear they have a shared vision and desire to return the Club to the Premier League as quickly as possible. I share that ambition and I’m very confident we can achieve it. I’ve been in this division three times and I’ve got out of this division three times. This is a tough division, there is absolutely no denying it. And I will use every ounce of my experience, every ounce of my knowledge, to have an understanding of what we’re going to need to bring consistency. And that’s going to be the key word for all of us really. The consistency of what we do and the commitment levels that we go to will give us the best opportunity to get out of this division and be the team that we can be.”

West Ham United Interim CEO Karim Virani: “We are delighted to welcome Scott and his family back to the Club. He is someone who is held in high regard at West Ham United and throughout the game, and he was the unanimous choice of the Board to become our new Head Coach. He has fantastic experience and pedigree across an outstanding playing and coaching career, a clear and proven track record of success as a Head Coach in the EFL Championship, and a deep understanding of West Ham United, its identity and our loyal and passionate fanbase. We believe that all of these factors together make him the right man to lead us forward and help the Club to achieve our objectives this season and beyond. Scott has the complete support of everyone here and, from the conversations we have had with him already, we believe he will represent West Ham United and our supporters in a way that we can all be extremely proud of.”

#2058. Arsenal news: Arteta’s side secure landmark victory at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal news, Arsenal have finally found a way to win at Anfield again. Their latest victory owed as much to defensive discipline as Kai Havertz’s decisive goal.

The Gunners claimed a 1-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool, ending their 14-year wait for victory at the iconic stadium. Declan Rice set up their opener as Havertz put the visitors ahead on the 16th minute.

It was a tough afternoon for Mikel Arteta’s side as they were put under sustained pressure by their opponents. The Reds also created a number of dangerous chances throughout the match, especially in the first half.

Arsenal held their composure, and the backline was calm throughout. David Raya made the crucial interventions to keep the lead safe.

They are now three points ahead at the top of the Premier League after Manchester City lost to Brighton.

While the attack has been a key aspect of Arsenal’s title charge, they were put under pressure defensively at Anfield.

Liverpool came out aggressively after going behind. Virgil van Dijk caused problems from set pieces, and Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar from a free kick.

Raya was quick to block Van Dijk’s dangerous flick on and prevent Alexander Isak from capitalising. However, Alexis Mac Allister did head over the bar as Liverpool looked to level the game.

Arsenal were forced into another stretch as Jurrien Timber blocked well. William Saliba and Gabriel helped to limit Liverpool’s chances.

The stats tell the story of how well the visitors defended. Liverpool had 17 shots but couldn’t get one on target.

Liverpool were unable to create a shot on target for the first time in recorded history (since 2003-04) in a Premier League game at Anfield.

Meanwhile, it was the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet in the Premier League at the ground since September 2012. The result was especially important following their Carabao Cup heartbreak against Fleetwood Town earlier in the week.

Whilst they have made a great defensive stand, Arsenal’s two most influential players in the final third made the difference.

Rice won the turnover, drove down the right and played a low cross into the six-yard box. Havertz made his run to the back post and finished to give Arsenal the early lead.

The goal also takes Havertz to 46 Premier League goals, making him the most prolific German in the competition and overtaking former Manchester City midfielder Ilkay Gündogan.

Rice had a huge influence on the game. His performance in the middle of the park helped Arsenal deal with the intensity of Liverpool, and he was named man of the match.

Christos Tzolis provided an important attacking outlet. His pace created chances to ease pressure on Arsenal. He forced an incredible save from Alisson with a late first-time effort.

The win was Arsenal’s first at Anfield in any competition since September 2012 and their 300th away win in the Premier League.

Arteta’s team have had a stellar start to the season, taking 24 points from nine games. They have also proved they are capable of getting results in tough circumstances.

They will now look ahead to their Champions League game on Wednesday against Slavia Prague and then back to domestic action against Hull City.

#2057. Arsenal injury news: Eberechi Eze concern emerges as Bukayo Saka awaits scan

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal came out on top in their match against Liverpool. Mikel Arteta admitted they have a new injury concern to deal with after Eberechi Eze was hurt. Bukayo Saka is also still out for the Gunners as they face two more games before the break.

The 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield means they are three points clear at the top of the Premier League. Arteta will need to be careful with his squad ahead of their Champions League clash against Slavia Prague on Wednesday and home game against Hull City.

Eze was a surprise omission from the starting line-up, despite featuring well in recent games.

Arteta later revealed that the England international was suffering from a problem going into the game. He also praised the club’s medical and performance team for getting him fit enough to be included in the travelling party.

There is some light at the end of the tunnel, with Eze being named on the bench. There is uncertainty over whether he will be available for the trip to Prague.

Arsenal will look to train him to see if he can play against Slavia. However, Arteta’s comments suggest that the issue is significant enough that he couldn’t start against Anfield despite his recent form.

There is positive news on Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori. All three were able to overcome their fitness concerns to start the game against Liverpool and play the full 90 minutes.

The availability of these players provides Arteta with more options as he heads into a busy week. However, he will be keen to avoid any unnecessary risk to those that have only just returned to full fitness.

Saka is still the biggest injury concern for Arsenal as he has failed to play for the last three games after suffering a quad injury in the clash against Bayern Munich.

He was forced off after just 10 minutes of the Champions League draw. He will not be available for the fixtures against Slavia Prague and Hull.

There were concerns that Saka may miss up to eight weeks of action. Arteta hasn’t confirmed when he will be back on the pitch.

The Arsenal manager explained earlier that there was a need to scan Saka again to see how the fluid around the injury was behaving. The medical staff will also want to know if there has been any damage to the tendon.

This will give clearer information on when he will be able to return to play. Until then Arsenal will have to plan without one of their most important attacking players.

Another player looking to make his way back to fitness is William Saliba. The defender has not played this season after aggravating a back issue during his time playing for France at the World Cup.

However, he has avoided surgery and has been back in individual outdoor training at the club’s training ground recently. Arteta says there are positive signs that his recovery is going well.

The club plan for an MRI scan to see how he is recovering. They are hoping to get him back in December, but it has not been confirmed by Arsenal.

It would give Arteta a huge boost to his defensive options. For now he will have to keep monitoring his recovery.

They play Slavia Prague on Wednesday and then play Hull at home on Saturday. This gives them two more chances to build up their position ahead of the international break; however, Arteta will have to consider the latest medical reports.

#2055. West Ham Exclusive: Nuno Meeting Brought Sacking Forward

Claret & Hugh can reveal this morning that West Ham United dismissed Nuno Espírito Santo earlier than originally planned following a meeting between the head coach and club executives on Monday morning.

West Ham had become increasingly concerned about results and performances, and Nuno’s position was already under considerable scrutiny. The club had sounded out various potential replacements, including Scott Parker, but the intention had been to assess the situation over the next two Championship fixtures against Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers.

However, that timetable changed following Monday’s meeting, during which Nuno would ordinarily have been expected to review the previous match and discuss plans for the January transfer window. Instead, the decision was taken to dismiss him with immediate effect, bringing his time at West Ham to an abrupt end.

As Claret & Hugh reported before Nuno’s dismissal, there had been growing concern within the club’s hierarchy about the direction of the team. However, the expectation had been that the Portuguese coach would have the Cardiff and Blackburn matches to demonstrate that he could turn things around.

That changed on Monday lunchtime. Quite what happened during the meeting has not been disclosed, but it would be fair to say that the outcome was not what Nuno would have been hoping for. Perhaps, and this is purely speculation on my part, he failed to provide the answers or assurances West Ham’s executives were seeking.

Whatever the precise circumstances, the decision meant Nuno would not be taking training on Tuesday morning. Instead, the club moved quickly to accelerate its search for a replacement, with Scott Parker emerging as the leading candidate to take charge.

Parker was rushing into West Ham ahead of schedule

The former Hammers midfielder was subsequently lined up for a two-and-a-half-year contract, with West Ham determined to have their new manager in place as quickly as possible.

As we revealed yesterday, Parker’s proposed agreement includes clauses linked to securing promotion back to the Premier League, while Nuno’s departure is expected to cost the club just under £3million in compensation.

The speed of the change has created an unusual situation ahead of tonight’s Championship trip to Cardiff City. Mark Noble has been overseeing preparations alongside Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville, although Claret & Hugh understands Parker will attend the match and could have some influence on team selection.

The rest, as they say, is history. West Ham had been preparing to give Nuno another two games, but Monday’s meeting brought that process to an unexpectedly early conclusion.

And while we may never discover precisely what was said behind closed doors, tonight’s trip to Wales provides an immediate opportunity for the players to put a dreadful couple of weeks behind them and begin moving forward under a new regime.

#2054. Arsenal transfer news: Arteta considers January moves for two highly rated attackers

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could have two ambitious attacking signings in mind for January. Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz are reportedly attracting Mikel Arteta’s attention.

Both players have emerged as potential targets as the Gunners consider further changes to their forward line. However, Arsenal may face a battle to prise either youngster away from their current club.

Kroupi is already familiar with the Premier League after making an impressive start to life at Bournemouth. The forward arrived from Lorient and scored 13 goals in 35 appearances across all competitions during his first season in England.

His development was halted by a broken foot in pre-season which required an operation to fix and kept him out of action for around three months.

The 20-year-old has now returned to the Bournemouth squad and has played as a substitute in their last three games. He will be hoping to get more game time as he gets back into full fitness.

Arsenal were linked with a move for Kroupi in the summer. His return to action has reignited interest in the player. A number of other European clubs also understood to be watching his situation.

Kroupi has attracted interest from a variety of top clubs including Manchester United, Tottenham, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

The French Under-21 international has impressed with his goal scoring in his first campaign in England. At only 20 years old, he has plenty of development to do under an experienced manager like Arteta.

However, Bournemouth are said to be reluctant to let Kroupi leave in January. Selling a bright young forward would leave Marco Rose with a tough decision to make.

It could get even more complicated if Alex Scott is also being seriously pursued. Chelsea and Liverpool are both linked with the midfielder.

Arsenal may therefore struggle to convince the Cherries to part with Kroupi during the winter window.

Another exciting option for Arsenal comes in the form of Juventus winger Yildiz. The winger has been linked with a move to North London for a number of transfer windows. He has once again been in the news recently at the end of the summer.

However, the Turkish international has struggled to get going on this campaign. He has only featured once in Serie A and has failed to feature since he suffered an injury.

Juventus have previously shown little interest in letting him leave. Head coach Luciano Spalletti firmly dismissed the prospect during the summer. Indicating that even an offer worth €100 million would not change the club’s position.

However, things could change next season. There are reports from Italy that Juventus may have to sell their star player if they fail to make the Champions League.

The Turin-based outfit are currently sitting in seventh spot in Serie A after just 10 games and are six points away from the qualifying spots.

This means that if they don’t make it into Europe, then it could put more pressure on Arsenal’s pursuit of Yildiz. It could create more pressure on them to raise funds.

Arsenal had a very busy summer with the addition of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier.

But they also missed out on a few big names, such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

Despite this, there is still interest in Kroupi and Yildiz, suggesting that Arteta is still looking to strengthen his attacking options. Both players would bring quality and potential to the squad; however, there are some issues with both.

There are many unknowns surrounding this situation. Bournemouth aren’t keen to sell Kroupi and Juventus aren’t in a great financial position.

This doesn’t mean that either player will definitely be moving to the Emirates but much will depend on what happens at their clubs in the coming months.

#2053. Arsenal U19s face tough Slavia Prague test in UEFA Youth League

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s under-19s face a significant challenge when they travel to Czechia to take on Slavia Prague in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday.

The young Gunners have picked up four points from their first three games and will be hoping to build on that in the league phase. Two wins would definitely help their chances of getting into the knockout stages.

They kicked off their campaign with a win against Napoli and put on a great show in a 3-3 draw against Bayern Munich last month.

Those results have left them 18th in the standings, 16 places below their next opponents. With the top 22 teams progressing to the knockout stages, another positive result could prove important for their qualification hopes.

However, Slavia Prague has made a much stronger start and will provide a difficult examination for David Horseman’s side.

Slavia have won all three of their first games in the UEFA Youth League and are sitting in second place. Just behind Real Madrid on goal difference.

They began well with a 2-1 win against French side Lens. They then went on to beat Sabah 3-0 and then put in another strong display against Fenerbahce.

Despite falling behind in Prague, the players fought back to win the game 3-1. The three wins means Slavia are already past the number of points they scored last season in the league stage.

They also advanced to the knockout stages last time, finishing 20th before they faced Benfica.

Mubarak Suleiman put the team ahead twice, but they were pegged back by two goals in the last 30 minutes as their European run came to an end.

This season they have looked like a much stronger team. With a perfect record, they will be one of the hardest teams that Arsenal will face.

The meeting on Wednesday provides an opportunity for Arsenal to get revenge for their heavy defeat in Prague last season.

The two sides met during the 2025/26 league campaign, with Slavia winning 5-1 at home.

Arsenal were three goals down at the break after an own goal plus goals from Bartosz Szywala and Jakub Kolisek.

O’Neill pulled one back after the break, but the home side had the final word as Suleiman and Matej Kotrba scored in stoppage time.

This loss shows how tough it will be for Horseman’s side. Slavia have already proven their attacking prowess against Arsenal and are playing even better in this campaign.

The young Gunners will have to play much more disciplined if they are to leave Prague with three points.

Arsenal fans can watch the UEFA Youth League clash on Wednesday.

It will be streamed via the Arsenal app and Arsenal.com, with the match taking place at the Sports Centre Radotin.

Updates will also be posted here and on the club’s Academy X page.

A full match report, highlights and post-match interviews with Horseman and one of the young players will be published on Arsenal’s official channels.

With them still in contention to qualify for the knockout stages, Arsenal will be looking to get off to a good start. Slavia’s great early start means they will have to play some of their best football of the tournament.

#2052. Scott Parker Confirmed As West Ham Boss – And He’s Ready For Cardiff

West Ham United have officially confirmed the appointment of Scott Parker as our new head coach, with the former Hammers captain signing a two-and-a-half-year contract. The announcement also confirms that Parker will take charge of tonight’s Championship fixture against Cardiff City, rather than Mark Noble, who had been overseeing preparations following Nuno Espírito Santo’s dismissal.

In a statement published on the official West Ham website, the club confirmed that Parker will be supported by Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, while Noble will work closely with his former teammate. Further details of the permanent coaching structure will be announced in due course.

Parker returns to West Ham having achieved promotion from the Championship with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. It’s an impressive record and, with the Hammers desperate to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, I think there are plenty of reasons to be excited about his appointment.

Speaking following his appointment, Parker made it clear just how much returning to West Ham means to him.

“It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a Club that means so much to me and my family.”

The new manager also spoke passionately about his determination to secure promotion, pointing to his previous Championship experience and the importance of bringing consistency to West Ham’s performances.

“I’ve been in this division three times and I’ve got out of this division three times.”

That experience is precisely what West Ham need at the moment, but it’s not the only reason I’m looking forward to seeing Parker in the dugout.

I’ve got to say, I’m pretty excited about Scott Parker coming in. He wouldn’t necessarily have been my first choice, but I think his passion and enthusiasm will represent a real change from the softly spoken Nuno Espírito Santo. West Ham are a club that need a demonstrative manager on the touchline, somebody who looks as though he’s kicking every ball alongside the players.

I want to see a manager who communicates, motivates and shows the same urgency that we expect from the team. Parker has always struck me as somebody who understands what West Ham means to its supporters, and I think that connection could be particularly important after a difficult few months.

As Nuno’s departure demonstrated, something needed to change at the London Stadium. Parker now has an immediate opportunity to lift the players, improve performances and get West Ham’s promotion campaign moving in the right direction.

There is also something reassuring about having Parker, Noble and Potts involved in the club’s footballing setup. They understand West Ham, they know what supporters expect, and there should be no shortage of passion in the dugout.

Of course, none of that guarantees results, but I’m pleased with the appointment. We’ve brought in somebody who knows the Championship, understands West Ham and genuinely wants to be here.

The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel has now given its verdict on two match moments concerning Newcastle United.

The KMI panel has five members, made up of three former players and/or coaches, plus one representative each from the Premier League and PGMOL (Now ‘Pro Ref’).

It was set up at the start of the 2022/23 season to give an independent assessment of decision-making rather than relying on the views of PGMOL or the clubs themselves.

The judgement is intended to provide an arm’s-length assessment of all major match incidents but gives weight to the decision of the referee in subjective situations, taking into account the laws of the game and the Premier League’s interpretation.

The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel have looked at the Crystal Palace v Newcastle United match that was played on Sunday 25 October 2026 and voted on these two incidents.

Incident in 18th minute: Challenge by Fabian Schar on Kamada in the penalty area.

KMI Panel: Panel voted 5-0 in support of that no penalty decision as ‘normal contact as both players are competing for the ball.’

Incident in 52nd minute: Joe Willock scores a goal.

Decision by match officials: VAR rules against it due to offside.

KMI Panel: Panel voted 5-0 in support of that no goal decision, unanimously adjudging it offside as well.

#2050. Arsenal handed major William Saliba injury boost ahead of Manchester City showdown

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have received a significant boost with William Saliba returning to first-team training. He’s spent almost four months out with a back injury.

The French international was seen returning to training on the pitch. Sparking hope that he could be back in action soon for Mikel Arteta.

Saliba has been sidelined since he suffered the injury in France’s 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain. The defender was forced off after only 30 minutes after playing the full 90 in his previous five starts at the tournament.

The player was confirmed by Arsenal to be sidelined for a lengthy period of time in July. He did not require surgery, meaning he can begin working back into action.

His latest progress comes at an important point in Arsenal’s season, with several major fixtures approaching.

The 25-year-old has travelled to the Czech Republic with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba had played for 45 minutes in a behind-closed-moors game last week as part of his rehab.

He then returned to full first team training on Tuesday, providing another defensive option for the club.

Arteta spoke ahead of the game against Slavia Prague. He said that Saliba is happy with his recovery and is at a point where he will be used if needed.

The Arsenal manager has not confirmed if the Frenchman will be involved tonight.

Saliba has not played in a competitive game since losing to Spain in the World Cup semi-final for France. So it will be his first involvement in a competitive game since the summer.

Arsenal have coped well with Saliba’s absence.

Gabriel initially partnered Cristhian Mosquera at centre-back before the Spaniard suffered an ankle injury. This allowed Ezri Konsa to come into the starting line-up.

Ezri Konsa settled into a partnership with the Brazilian. He joined from Aston Villa for £51 million in the summer.

The partnership has helped the Gunners to have the best defensive record in the Premier League. Having only conceded 5 goals in their first 9 games.

Now that Saliba is available, Arteta has more options and flexibility with his defenders.

The manager has had past success with Saliba and Gabriel as his first-choice central defensive pairing. Their understanding has played a big part in Arsenal’s defensive displays.

However, Konsa has provided Arteta with another selection dilemma to consider when Saliba is back to full fitness.

Arsenal have a busy schedule ahead after today’s Champions League game at Slavia Prague.

On Saturday they play Hull City, followed by games against Manchester City, Real Madrid and Tottenham after the international break in November.

If Saliba can come back in, it will give Arteta more defensive options to play with, but they won’t want to rush him back.

The defender played 50 times last season, helping Arsenal win the Premier League and reach the Champions League final. He also ranked 29th in the men’s Ballon d’Or in October.

His return to training is a major step in his road to full fitness, but it remains to be seen if he will play against Slavia Prague tonight.

#2049. West Ham Had No Choice But to End the Nuno Era – Here’s Why

“Stale.” It’s a simple word, but one that perfectly sums up the final months of Nuno Espírito Santo’s reign at West Ham United.

The football had become predictable, uninspiring and, all too often, difficult to watch. What arrived with optimism and expectation slowly descended into frustration and stagnation, leaving us supporters increasingly detached from a side that looked incapable of building momentum.

A win rate of just 35.8%, made up of 19 victories, 19 defeats and 15 draws, is hardly the return expected from a manager reportedly earning a basic £4.5 million per year. Add in performance-related bonuses that could have taken that figure beyond £5.5 million and the value for money argument becomes even harder to defend.

Much has already been written about Nuno’s career, his close relationship with football super-agent Jorge Mendes and his previous managerial successes and failures. However, the issues at West Ham appeared to run far deeper than results alone.

Reports of dressing-room unrest became increasingly difficult to ignore. The reaction from several players on social media following the club’s announcement of Nuno’s departure painted a picture that suggested not everyone was disappointed to see the back of the Portuguese coach.

Whether fair or not, perceptions matter, and by the time the board made its decision, it appeared they had little room left to manoeuvre.

Frequent tactical changes, constant rotation and regular shifts in formation left players struggling to develop understanding and rhythm. Too often the team looked unsure of its identity. One week brought a back three, the next a back four. Players found themselves moved in and out of the side without any obvious continuity.

The consequence was a team that never truly settled.

That is not to absolve the players of responsibility. Several underperformed throughout the campaign, regardless of the system being deployed. Ultimately, however, modern football remains a results business and the head coach is invariably the man held accountable when things go wrong.

Rightly or wrongly, that responsibility now sits firmly in the past.

The former Bournemouth and Burnley manager arrives with a clear brief, reignite confidence, restore belief and turn one of the Championship’s most talented squads into a genuine automatic promotion contender.

The challenge is significant, but so is the opportunity.

Tonight’s fixture against Cardiff City comes too early for Parker to have much influence, with the interim coaching team of Potts, Robson, Noble and Prenderville overseeing proceedings. However, it offers the first step in what supporters hope will be a fresh start.

The Nuno Espírito Santo chapter closes with disappointment, underachievement and a lingering sense of what might have been. Whether the blame lies with the manager, the players, or both, the reality is simple: The project failed to deliver.

Now comes the hard part. West Ham’s season is still alive, but the margin for error has all but disappeared. If promotion is to be achieved, the talent within this squad must finally translate into performances on the pitch.

The Nuno era ended exactly as it had become, Stale.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Your article suggests that Mark Robson is now part of Scott Parker’s first team coaching group. I had been concerned that he had been omitted from the group on the official site
