#2048. Newcastle United Women’s team tear woeful Wearsiders apart

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The Newcastle United Women’s team went into their latest League Cup game looking for their first win in the competition this season, with three defeats from three group games (of six in total) so far.

Manager Tanya Oxtoby selected a strong side to take on what was a pitiful Durham side at South Shields, as the Lasses collected their first points in the Subway Players League Cup.

The Newcastle United Women’s team scored five goals for the first time under Tanya Oxtoby as they tore the woeful Wearsiders apart.

However, despite the visitors dominating from kick-off Durham did take a shock lead on 14 minutes when a scramble in front of goal from Lucy Watson’s corner wasn’t cleared and United goalie Kayla Rendell was unable to keep it out at the near post with the ball somewhat fortuitously crept over the line.

Durham were buoyed by that goal and started to play more physically going forward, leaving themselves exposed at the back, which played perfectly into the hands of Newcastle who started to tear them apart.

Newcastle were effective at moving the ball quickly and nearly took the lead when top scorer Martha Thomas was played through before drawing two defenders with her. A clever back heel set up the on-rushing Beth Lumsden in the area but her strike lacked accuracy and sailed wide of the far post.

With the Lasses finding their groove and Durham left appealing for offside, Lumsden pounced and raced towards the byline, before setting up Kathleen McGovern from six yards out, but the Scottish international was inches away from making contact.

Their persistence finally paid off though soon after and they were level by the mid-point of the half. Thomas latched onto a defence-splitting pass from Mollie Lambert, racing through on goal, holding off Durham captain Sarah Wilson before guiding her effort into the far corner.

Durham’s goal scorer tried her luck again soon after as she shot from the edge of the box and forced Rendell into a low save, with the ball squibbing free and only just going around the post. Perhaps two slices of luck were too much to ask for by the home side.

Straight away Newcastle went back on the attack. From a quickly taken throw-in Thomas found Lumsden in space, with the flying winger able to run and cut the ball back to Jordan Nobbs who looked to have swept home only for the ball to narrowly drift wide.

But with less than ten minutes before half time Newcastle eventually grabbed their go-ahead goal. Nobbs was at the heart of it as she picked out Lumsden down the left flank who in turn cut inside onto her weaker foot and curled home in off the far post for 2-1.

Nobbs could have made it a two goal advantage just before the break as she was found between two defenders. But her cross could only be glanced on by Thomas who hit the underside of the bar.

Five minutes into the second half and the Lasses did have their third goal. Lumsden turned inside Grace Ede before sending in an inch perfect cross for Thomas who slipped past her marker and volleyed home from twelve yards out.

It soon became 4-1 when Nobbs found Lumsden on the edge of the box, before the latter allowed the ball to bounce and fired home with Durham’s goalie Anna King powerless to stop it.

The scoring was complete when a Katie Bradley corner was sliced by Jade Pennock into her own net.

A truly comprehensive victory against a side still looking for their first points in either competition this season. Although perhaps Durham can always say they have appeared on hit TV show Ted Lasso.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Charlotte Wardlaw, Gemma Evans, Aoife Mannion, Kaitlyn Torpey, Lois Joel, Mollie Lambert (Hildur Antonsdóttir 83), Jordan Nobbs (Katie Bradley 65), Beth Lumsden (Oona Sevenius 65), Kathleen McGovern (Jessie Gale 65), Martha Thomas (Freya Gregory 59).

Subs not used: Soffia Kelly, Jemma Purfield, Emilia Larsson, Abbie Richardson

Durham: Anna King, Grace Ayre, Sarah Wilson, Lauren Briggs, Amber Keegan Stobbs, Eloise Morran (Rachel Lowe 74), Beth Hepple, Grace Ede (Angela Addison 74), Lucy Watson (Dee Bradley 74), Jade Pennock, Grace Collinson (Olivia Fergusson 59).

Subs not used: Cat Sheppard, Maddy McComasky, Lucy Noble, Emma Brown

Where that leaves Newcastle United Women’s team

Despite Newcastle’s emphatic win, it’s still unlikely they will progress to the knockout stages of this cup competition.

They have two games remaining, albeit both at home, but one is against runaway leaders Manchester United.

Back to the important stuff and top of the second tier Newcastle return to League action on Sunday, 8th November with Burnley set to visit at St James’ Park.

It will be the first of seven scheduled games at SJP this season.

After six matches of a 22 game league season, the Newcastle United Women’s team are top on 16 points.

It is vital they end the season there, as only the team that finishes top will be guaranteed promotion to the Super League.

#2047. Real Madrid welcomes sporting royalty as tennis icon joins board of directors

Tennis star Rafael Nadal has become a director of Real Madrid.

The club’s board met on Wednesday and agreed to submit to the general assembly of delegate members ratification of Nadal’s appointment as a new member of the board.

Nadal won 22 grand slam singles titles in a stellar career, including a record 14 French Open crowns. He retired from the sport in 2024.

A club statement described Nadal as “one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world”.

The statement added: “For Real Madrid and for all Madridismo it is a great pride that a figure of his sporting and human dimension, a benchmark in Spanish and world sport, becomes part of our board of directors and contributes, from this responsibility, to the present and future of our club.”

Real’s statement continued: “With his extraordinary track record, with 92 individual titles, including 22 grand slams, two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cups with Spain and number one in the world ranking, Rafael Nadal has starred in a legendary sporting career.

“But his figure represents much more than his successes: his talent, his spirit of permanent improvement, his capacity for sacrifice, his competitiveness, his humility, his respect for rivals and his team-mates, and his commitment to solidarity make him an example on and off the courts.

“All these values are part of Real Madrid’s identity, and Rafael Nadal has represented and defended them throughout his sporting life, becoming a reference for millions of people around the world.”

Nadal has spoken about his love of Real Madrid since childhood in previous interviews, despite his uncle Miguel Angel Nadal having played for their bitter rivals Barcelona.

Nadal has held honorary membership of Real for years, regularly attending matches at the Bernabeu. He was a guest of honour at the 2022 Champions League final in Paris when Real won their 14th Champions League title.

2026 is becoming something of a landmark year for West Ham United. Relegation, explosive allegations, departures, resignations, board room battles, a takeover foiled and now a manager sacked by telephone: It isn’t dull, is it.

Few fans would have expected the West Ham leadership to act so decisively, having grown accustomed to the slow painful, managerial death of a thousand ‘last games’ which had become West Ham’s preferred method of drawing out their head coach sackings.

Appointing a former three-time Hammer of the Year as head coach has certainly energised a fan base desperate for the end of the no-no-Nuno era.

Scott needs to hit the ground running. A pragmatic approach to getting the best out of the squad we have is vitally important.

Nuno was still playing around with nuanced differences and his plan was to get some out and get some more in in January to continue building ‘his’ team.

We did not have the time for this plan. We need the team to perform now. Come on Scotty!

Newcastle United fans with the latest collection of opinions below.

Contributions are sometimes too brief to make up into a full article.

Or sometimes a lot of varying views coming in on the same subject…

So we have gathered up a number of recent views sent in, (if you would like to send anything in, long or short, regarding Newcastle United, then contribute@themag.co.uk is the place):

Ross Wilson, Sporting Director at NUFC, needs to be held accountable for appointing a manager way out of his depth.

Wilson himself is clueless, as seen with the majority of summer signings he has sanctioned.

If big money signings are not ready for first team action, don’t sign them.

NUFC are not in a position to await the possibility of them becoming first team regulars in a year or two down the line.

I am guessing plenty of Newcastle United fans are embarrassed (well they should be!!!) now about the disrespect they showed to Eddie Howe in the second half of last season.

We had a brilliant elite manager and yet these idiots helped drive him away.

Eddie Howe faced a ridiculous impossible job last season after the Newcastle United owners totally wrecked his pre-season, especially when it came to the summer 2025 transfer window.

It was total dereliction of duty from the owners not to have a CEO or Sporting Director actively working at the club in summer 2025 to help get the deals for Eddie Howe’s top transfer targets done.

Instead of doing business with Liverpool, selling them the Rat and then they would have stepped aside to allow us to get Ekitike, we had the NUFC owners saying no way Isak would leave, only at the last minute to do exactly that! The damage already done as Eddie Howe had been waiting for his striker targets to get done. Only to have last minute Woltemade and Wissa signings which were NOT his top targets.

Indeed, I don’t think Big Nick was EVER on Eddie’s radar.

Just a case of having lost Isak and Wilson, Howe told it was Woltemade or nothing at the last minute.

All the talk about Newcastle United and the way we are playing.

Who is to blame, the manager or the players?

The manager picks the line up and game plan for each game, the players try to keep to that game plan.

Clueless in the final third, clueless man marking, defensive errors resulting in loss points.

Have the players lost confidence in the style of game plan they have been given by the manager?

Should they question the manager and tell him his plan is not working?

We all know it’s not the Newcastle United of two or three years ago.

Good players were sold under the nose of Eddie Howe.

To me that meant enough was enough for Eddie, goodbye.

Lets go one step higher to the Head Honchos, are they to blame for the mess?

So start at the top and work down to sift the issue.

Being a lifelong fan of the toon I was really pleased when the club was taken over and Eddie Howe appointed manager.

It was great, we had some success, more than we ever had in years, seemed like we had a club that could progress, even with a few hiccups.

That was until the club decided to put profit before anything else.

The fans didn’t want Alexander Isak to leave.

The fans didn’t want Anthony Gordon to leave.

The fans didn’t want Sandro Tonali to leave along with other good players.

Most certainly, the majority of fans did not want Eddie Howe to leave.

But the club simply ignored the fans and their promises to complete the plan.

The fans don’t want the current inexperienced manager who is seemingly dragging us down to a certain relegation fight, the fans want a proven Prem manager but it looks likely we will be ignored again.

In today’s football the toon being relegated wouldn’t really be a financial hardship for the club, certainly not for the owners.

The only ones who will suffer will be the fans.

I am totally disillusioned and I’m simply not gonna bother and let myself suffer through false hope.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly trying to protect the young players. Young signings made by Ross Wilson.

We saw the ridiculous over the top abuse Fernandez-Pardo got from many fans when Jaissle was forced to start him in a run of games far too early, due to so many injuries.

MFP just needs time and confidence and will be a very good player given time and support.

No wonder Jaissle has been reluctant to start Steur (who is only EIGHTEEN!) on a regular basis, he got abuse from many fans when making that naive mistake at Leeds for their second killer goal.

So many of these fans who are saying Jaissle is clueless because he is not starting Steur, would be the first ones to be giving the 18-year-old abuse if the teenager struggled.

(ED: This was received after the defeat to Aston Villa)

It is with regret I write this as I am a Toon man since 1940 and always, yes always, supported the team and the manager when under pressure.

Yesterday’s game vs Aston Villa showed the team to be poor, moving towards being very poor, in its overall performance on the park.

When I look at the recent performances of Bruno, Gordon, Isak (yes Isak!!), less so Tonali, I see what Newcastle let go and why my team for the last 87 years are heading catastrophically for relegation.

The new ‘exciting’ players have with the greatest respect, shown a total inability to put the ball in the net, create chances to put the ball in the net and equally as important to stop the opponents putting the ball in Wor net.

Never mind it’s ‘early days’, ‘settling into Premiership style’ etc etc. nonsense.

At £50+ million they are paid to put the ball in the net on a regular basis.

The recent German centre forward (joke here) is a classic example of what extremely poor judgement was shown at the top.

Never mind, as long as silly people like myself buy season tickets, pay for expensive lunches, players will privately laugh all the way to the bank. No passionate liking for the area (ask how many fly to London or stay in London after a game).

They are the 21st century carpet baggers and a total disgrace to my team which I have supported wholeheartedly for over 85 years. The next three games are critical. Lose and down we go. A long way to Portsmouth and Bristol City.

#2044. Revealed – when Nuno lost the West Ham dressing room

There’s a sense of deja vu for those reading of West Ham’s latest managerial casualty – the fourth since 2023- and what seems an overriding sense of relief amongst supporters that the end of the Nuno era has been delivered in a timely, swift, ruthless and businesslike manner.

Jacob Steinberg writing in the Guardian has confirmed how the dissatisfaction inside the club led to Daniel Kretinsky choosing to act decisively over dissatisfaction with Nuno’s performance, and the truth behind last weekend’s whispers that Nuno had lost the confidence of his players:

“Kretinsky has assumed more power and is said to have been unhappy with Nuno after attending West Ham’s 3-2 defeat by Southampton at the London Stadium.

Daniel Kretinsky decided to at decisively and with customary swiftness

There was further disquiet in the directors’ box when West Brom handed West ham a second consecutive home defeat. Kretinsky has recognised it was a mistake to stick with Nuno, who is due £3m in compensation…

While West Ham’s squad is far from perfect, the internal view is results should be better this season, especially as Nuno was able to break the EFL transfer record by spending £22m on Arne Engels from Celtic last summer. It is understood Nuno lost support in the dressing room in recent weeks. Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, was especially unhappy with him”

Other sources claim the West Bromwich defeat last weekend when ‘the mood darkened’ was the moment the dressing room turned – along with the fan base, judging from the boos at London Stadium.

Credit to West Ham for acting swiftly and decisively whilst thirty three games remain to make good on the head start they’ve given their Championship rivals.

#2043. Why this season feels so uncertain as a Newcastle United fan

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Hope you are all doing well, I am in my 40s and a long time Newcastle United fan living in Australia.

I eventually got the chance in September to come and see my first game at St James’ Park against Hull – it was brilliant.

I watch all the matches, read, listen to pods etc and have played all my life (I’m 42).

I’m also into the tactical side of things and have undertaken some of my coaching badges here in Australia.

I’m sharing my first submission to The Mag about why I think this season feels so uncertain as a Newcastle United fan.

Newcastle United are a club of ups and downs – we all know that. The club’s current reality feels like we’re on the way down, though in reality it is more like a straight line from last season than any sort of significant change :

2026/27 13th place in the Premier League after 9 games. 11 points in those 9 games at an average of 1.22 points per game. 2025/26 12th place in the Premier League after 38 games. 49 points in those 38 games at an average of 1.28 points per game.

There are lots of reasons that this season feels more ominous than last season, though primarily it’s because we have no clear idea what to expect from this manager and from this group and players. We don’t know what to expect.

For Newcastle United fans, this season is full of unknowns.

Was Eddie Howe keeping our heads above water?

Who on earth are half of these new players?

Could we… go down, or could we actually end up being alright with a few tweaks?

Never in recent years have Newcastle United fans had so much to be uncertain about.

Under the management of Eddie Howe, there was certainty. We knew him and he knew us. There was no chance we were getting relegated under Howe, even through last season’s struggles.

We knew he knew the league. We knew he knew how to win games in this league. We knew he knew the histories, we knew he knew just what a cold, wet night in Stoke meant. We knew he could (mostly) improve players on an individual basis and get the best out of them. We knew the players respected him, liked him and trusted him. We knew his tactics and his style, and we knew they worked (mostly).

We knew Howe’s team. We knew that when the chips were down, Bruno would take the lead. We knew he’d demand the ball, that he’d try with every last ounce of determination and skill to create something, to inspire his teammates and to inspire the fans. We knew big Joe had his back and would kick someone if he had to, or even if he didn’t. We knew we had a threat up front or out wide to hurt opponents. We knew we had guys who could score goals in the Premier League. We knew Tripps wouldn’t stand for a team that didn’t give their all. We knew we had high standards, kept by high quality players who had done it all and seen it all.

Now, all that safety and certainty is gone and you know what – it’s freaking us out. Without the guard-rails that the certainty of Howe provided for us, we’re contemplating the worst. We’re scared of free fall. We’re not cautiously optimistic – we’re venturing towards riotously pessimistic.

So, now, after a similar start to last season in terms of points, we’re worried. Not worried like we were last year – this time it’s different. We’re worried because we’ve got no idea what comes next. We’ve got no idea how Matthias Jaissle responds or what he might do to get a tune out of this team. We’ve got no real indication yet that this group of players can actually deliver at this level, under any manager.

We don’t know how PIF, David Hopkinson and Ross Wilson will respond to this, because they haven’t had to before. We don’t fully know whether they even know what they’re doing to be honest. They seem to for the most part, but here we are nine league games in, with fingernails dwindling, a hard run of games ahead and a bunch of youngsters or also rans to take us through to the derby and Christmas and the crazy winter schedule..,so maybe they don’t know what they’re doing?

So, while we gaze into the unknown, let’s also think about the knowns. We know we’ve got a great set of fans. We know that when St James’ Park is rocking we can get the team over the line against almost anyone. We know this year they might well need that and they’ll need us behind them to succeed in this league.

We know we’re in transition. We know we care. We know we want the team to succeed whoever the manager is, wherever he’s from and whoever is on the pitch. We know it’s going to be turbulent because when has it ever not been? And we also know, we don’t want to support anyone else.

#2042. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

It is all over in north London and Tottenham have booked their place in the third round of the League Cup with a comfortable 5-1 win over Charlton.

Newcastle have just about got past West Brom, winning 3-2 in the end, and they book their place in the third round.

At least the travelling Charlton fans have something to cheer about even if their side are being dumped out of the League Cup. A corner from the left comes to the back post, where Jones rises highest to head it between Kinsky’s legs and into the Tottenham net.

Savio thinks he has his second in quick succession but it will go down as Davies’ goal. Savio’s shot was on target but it deflects off Davies and goes in for Tottenham’s fifth on the night.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#2039. Celtic handed major injury boost as key star returns to training

Celtic have been handed a timely Europa League boost with Yang Hyun-jun returning to training ahead of Thursday night’s clash with Besiktas.

The South Korean winger is back with the first-team group after recovering from the hamstring problem that has kept him on the sidelines.

His return gives Martin O’Neill another attacking option as the club look to get their first points on the board in this season’s Europa League.

Yang was managing the injury while on international duty as South Korea went on to claim the Asian Games title. The 24-year-old was selected as an overage player for the tournament but was forced to miss the latter stages.

O’Neill had indicated last week that Yang was closing in on a return. He said: “He starts back with us on Monday; we’ll see how he is before the beginning of the international break.”

Celtic learn match officials for Besiktas and Kilmarnock home double-header

Celtic's record transfer handed surprising ‘doesn’t matter’ goals verdict

Ex-Celtic star backs 'amazing' former boss to deliver amid growing pressure

The Celtic boss must now decide whether the winger is ready to be thrown straight back into action against Besiktas or eased back into the fold.

Yang had been enjoying an impressive run before suffering the setback, and his return could provide a welcome lift for O’Neill.

Celtic have used a number of different options in the wide areas, with Haissem Hassan and Camilo Duran featuring on the right and Callum Osmand and Jota among those utilised from the opposite flank.

Yang’s last appearance for Celtic came in the 2-1 Premiership victory over St Mirren, when he found the net.

He could also come up against a familiar face on Thursday, with former Celtic striker and South Korea team-mate Oh Hyeon-gyu now part of the Besiktas squad.

#2038. Total Premier League minutes played by the 8 Newcastle United signings tells a story

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

A lot of focus on the eight Newcastle United signings that were brought in across summer 2026.

There were actually nine in total but teenager Ousmane Diabate was instantly loaned back to the selling club in Turkey in order to get regular first team football.

So what about these eight Newcastle United signings that have gone straight into the first team squad?

I have had a look at the minutes played so far this 2026-27 season by the new players.

Specifically, the minutes that each of the eight have played in the Premier League.

I think it tells a very clear story now we are nine Premier League matches (810 minutes) into this 2026-27 season.

Total Premier League minutes (out of a possible total of 810) played by the eight Newcastle United signings with breakdown match by match (Ev Everton, CP Crystal Palace, AV Aston Villa, Cov Coventry, H Hull, Le Leeds, B Bournemouth, T Tottenham, Li Liverpool):

0 Ewen Jaouen (Zero minutes in any of the nine Premier League matches)

115 Bazoumana Toure (3Ev, 34AV, 30Cov, 16H, 33Le)

256 Sean Steur (26Ev, 5CP, 66H, 71 Le, 13B, 19T, 56Li)

304 Matias Fernandez-Pardo (56AV, 90Cov, 74H, 57Le, 27B)

501 Nico Gonzalez (64Ev, 90CP, 90AV, 90Cov, 19Le, 77B, 71T)

536 Amar Dedic (87Ev, 90CP, 31Cov, 58Le, 90B, 90T, 90Li)

810 Lukas Hornicek (90Ev, 90CP, 90AV, 90Cov, 90H, 90Le, 90B, 90T, 90Li)

What stands out for me, is that Matthias Jaissle has given far more Premier League minutes to the (relatively) older and more experienced Newcastle United signings.

Three of the eight Newcastle United signings were aged 24 when they arrived, the other five were 21 or under.

Lukas Hornicek has played every Premier League minute this season.

Nico Gonzalez has started all seven EPL matches he has been available for.

Amar Dedic has started all of the EPL matches he was in a position to start, as well as off the bench against Coventry.

The other five Newcastle United signings who were aged 21 and under when they arrived at St James’ Park, have played 702 minutes between them. That is less than Lukas Hornicek alone has played and would also be less than the Dedic and Gonzalez individual totals if they had been available all of the time.

On the other hand, Matias Fernandez-Pardo has played far more minutes than I think he would have otherwise done so far, simply because of so many injured players in the early part of the season.

I am sure that Matthias Jaissle sees the exciting potential of Sean Steur just as much as we do, probably even more so considering he watches him every day in training. However, my belief is that the Head coach is simply trying to protect the 18-year-old from too much expectancy and pressure too soon. The same with the other younger players.

I don’t think he is holding the likes of Toure and Bamba back from playing more minutes so far because of any negative irrational reason, more a case of giving these younger inexperienced players from weaker leagues a chance to integrate and build up their confidence rather than throwing them in at the deep end and a case of sink or swim?

The booing from many Newcastle United fans at the Everton match for example, it isn’t exactly something that will help younger players to build confidence if they are subjected to that.

#2036. Spectacular finish as supersub Sean Neave turns it around for Wolves with his first ever goals

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

What a night for Newcastle United teenage loan star Sean Neave at Wolves.

With Wolves chasing promotion back to the Premier League and still with much of the squad that was relegated from the top tier, Sean Neave has found it difficult to get much time on the pitch in the Championship.

Sitting on the bench once again tonight, the 19-year-old Newcastle United fan watched on as Wolves trailed 1-0 to Bristol City.

Nine minutes later and Neave’s former United teammate Kieran Trippier volleyed a cross in from the right, fellow Newcastle fan and former NUFC striker Adam Armstrong saw his first-time shot saved, only for Sean Neave to pounce and net the rebound.

A first ever goal in senior football for Sean Neave and earning Wolves a valuable point.

However…with only one minute of normal time remaining, Wolves captain Kieran Tripper put in a free-kick, Ladislav Krejci headed it back across goal and Sean Neave headed the winner!

The Geordie teenager from Winlaton has had to bide his time and keep working hard in training, his first ever goals in senior football.

Sean Neave has still only played 153 minutes of Championship football but now has two goals and an assist.

Thanks to their loan striker, Wolves move up to second in the table and Middlesbrough now only a point ahead of them.

#2035. Player Ratings West Ham v Cardiff: Bowen Inspires Incredible Comeback

West Ham produced an extraordinary second-half comeback to rescue a 3-3 draw against Cardiff City, having looked completely shell-shocked as they trudged off at half-time three goals behind. Scott Parker’s first game in charge certainly wasn’t short of incident, with the Hammers seemingly heading for another humiliating defeat.

Joel Moylan’s first-half hat-trick had left West Ham in all sorts of trouble, but three substitutions at the interval helped transform the performance. Goals from Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman completed a remarkable recovery, with the Hammers almost snatching a winner during a frantic finish.

Jarrod Bowen was the inspiration behind the comeback, although the difference between West Ham’s first and second-half performances was astonishing. Having looked completely devoid of confidence during the opening 45 minutes, the players suddenly discovered some urgency, purpose and attacking quality.

It was certainly a dramatic response to the dreadful performance against West Bromwich Albion, although Parker will have seen plenty of problems that still need addressing.

Made a couple of decent saves and produced one absolutely brilliant long throw that almost released Castellanos. Had little chance with Cardiff’s opening goal, but his decision to charge out of his penalty area, miss the ball completely and collide with Kilman was unnecessarily rash. Another unconvincing performance.

Steady and assured defensively in the first half, but his understanding with Bowen was almost nonexistent. The pair looked like they’d never met each other before. Completely different after the break, when Veltman played with real intensity, provided attacking width and combined excellently with the captain. One of West Ham’s most improved performers.

Some excellent defending, including a particularly impressive one-on-one challenge late in the game. His distribution was also a major positive, regularly pinging accurate balls towards the left flank and producing a lovely through ball to create Kanté’s one-on-one opportunity. One of West Ham’s better players across the 90 minutes.

Made an excellent early tackle but was subsequently booked after Solomon’s dreadful loss of possession exposed the defence. May have got a slight deflection on Cardiff’s opening goal, although there was little he could realistically have done. More than made amends in the 81st minute, showing West Ham’s strikers how to finish with a superb half-volley to equalise.

Actually started very well, winning numerous tackles and recovering possession repeatedly. Unfortunately, his lack of pace was badly exposed by a simple ball over the top, leading to a clumsy and avoidable penalty. He’s a centre-back being asked to play left-back, and it showed. Replaced at half-time.

Made his fair share of tackles and demonstrated some of the value of having a specialist defensive midfielder. Produced a crucial last-ditch challenge to prevent Cardiff from potentially scoring again. However, West Ham still left far too much space in central areas and he was withdrawn at half-time.

Worked hard in a box-to-box role but offered surprisingly little of note for much of the match. Played a decent pass in the build-up to one of Kanté’s attacking runs before making a beautifully timed run beyond Cardiff’s defence to score his first West Ham goal. Took the finish very well, and it was a significant contribution.

West Ham’s most technically accomplished player in the first half, looking comfortable in possession and enjoying the freedom of playing as a number ten. Picked out some lovely passes, including an excellent through ball that Castellanos couldn’t capitalise upon. Took his goal brilliantly, controlling Bowen’s chipped pass with his right foot before finishing delicately with his left. A very encouraging performance.

His performance was a microcosm of West Ham’s entire evening. Anonymous and nervous in the first half, but absolutely commanding in the second. His clever chipped pass created Mukasa’s goal, his long ball started the move for Engels’ strike, and his inswinging delivery provided the equaliser for Kilman.

By the closing stages he was practically running the game, producing a wonderful piece of jiggery-pokery to create a late chance for Mayers before delivering another dangerous inswinging ball that Souček headed on target. Outstanding after the break.

Showed some early purpose with a good run down the left, but his decision-making was dreadful. Repeatedly hesitated when presented with opportunities to shoot or pass, and one particularly poor three-yard ball straight to an opponent led to Kilman’s booking. His final deliveries were ineffective and he struggled to make the most of promising positions. Replaced after 67 minutes, and not before time.

Pretty much anonymous throughout the first half. Repeatedly outpaced when through balls offered him opportunities to run beyond Cardiff’s defence, including one occasion when he was beaten for speed by centre-back Will Fish. Managed a tame shot just before the interval but offered very little. Admittedly, West Ham’s disjointed attacking play hardly helped him. Replaced at half-time.

At least attempted to drop deep and get involved, although his first couple of contributions involved giving the ball away. Headed a decent Veltman cross straight at Trott and failed to connect properly with another Bowen delivery. Improved considerably, producing a good shot from distance before supplying an excellent flick-on for Engels’ goal.

Brought tremendous energy and directness after coming on at half-time. Produced an excellent driving run almost half the length of the pitch, followed by some lovely footwork to twist and turn through Cardiff’s defence. Gave the ball away cheaply on occasion but also forced Trott into a very good save after a wonderful first touch created a one-on-one opportunity. Probably did enough to force his way into Parker’s thoughts for the next game.

Introduced at half-time to replace Morato and provide some much-needed pace at full-back. Won an early tackle and looked more comfortable dealing with the demands of the position. Almost scored a dramatic late winner after making an excellent run to meet Bowen’s chipped delivery at the far post, attempting a left-footed instep volley that went tantalisingly close.

Made more of an attacking impression in his first 30 seconds than Solomon had managed for much of the evening. Immediately dropped his shoulder, cut inside and tried his luck with a shot that went wide. In the 89th minute, produced a stinging effort that Trott could only parry back into his penalty area. Confident, positive and willing to take responsibility.

Introduced in the 88th minute for Veltman. Almost scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner when he met another dangerous inswinging Bowen delivery with a well-directed header, forcing Nathan Trott into an excellent save. Not on the pitch long enough to warrant a numerical rating.

#2034. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool will be in pot one, while Manchester United and Aston Villa will be in pot two.

This evening’s ceremony should be getting underway in Monaco in a couple of minutes.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Gabriel misses his penalty ❌PSG WIN THE UEFA CHAMPIONS LEAGUE!!! 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/6XSuU3xqsN

Cristiano Ronaldo 🖐️#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/WzeWLfEomZ

Guendouzi provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch in the aftermath of a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium that sent the Turkish outfit through to the Champions League group stage.

Matteo Guendouzi has not forgotten who his rivals are... 👀The former Marseille player made his feelings known as Fenerbahce knocked out Marseille's rivals Lyon. pic.twitter.com/pjDKPqPzZD

As he gestured towards the fans, while being shepherded by team-mates, objects were thrown from the crowd. A figure in what appears to be a Lyon tracksuit then emerged from the tunnel and seemed to try to aim a flying kick at Guendouzi.

Of the 36 teams in the draw, 29 qualified at the end of last season, while the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.

AEK, LASK, Viking, Slovan Bratislava, Sabah Baku, Fenerbahce and Bodo/Glimt were the seven teams to come through the play-offs.

#2033. Cardiff City 3 – 3 West Ham | Final whistle, first impressions

IT took all of eleven minutes for the new manager bubble to burst as the home side opened the scoring and the Cardiff City fans duly launched into ‘you’re getting sacked in the morning’ to welcome West Ham’s Scott Parker into the dugout. To be fair, a cracking strike from Jack Moylan gave Hermansen no chance and as is now customary, the Hammers found themselves playing catch up.

Parker’s West Ham had set up with a back four holding a surprisingly high line, plus Magassa and Engels playing in front of the defenders but the pair were still bisected by the excellent pass that put Moylan through for his goal.

New manager, same misery as three went in before half time – again

Magassa and Kilman went into the book early on, the young Frenchman in particular looking short of match pace. Taty looked isolated – as we’d feared – and the Hammers looked a little short of ideas the half hour mark, hardly venturing into their opponent’s 18 yard box.

The warning signs were there as the awful Morato was beaten a couple of times as the Bluebirds attacked down the left: The stand in left back duly gave away a penalty, again out of position and clambering all over the back of his winger. Two-nil with Hermansen again beaten from a spot kick.

A third came from a corner, headed in at the near post by Moylan – a hat trick in the first half – and Scott Parker might have been questioning his rush to assume control ahead of the international break: Three nil before half time, three goals conceded for a third week in a row and the Hammers booed off by their own fans again.

Piroe warming up with Kanté and Mayers showed three changes at half time as Magassa, Morato and Taty departed.

Mukasa’s lobbed goal after being put through by Bowen put the Irons back in the game, with still half an hour to go and at least giving the travelling supporters something to cheer. Bowen, playing more centrally, started to pull the strings and Piroe went close. Suddenly, from nothing, a Bowen through pass was flicked on by Piroe and Engles, through on goal slotted home like a veteran striker. 3-2: And thousands of Hammers armchair fans were thinking maybe, just maybe.

This was, at least, a fighting response to a half time dressing down and a well deserved barracking from the away fans.

Kanté almost levelled down one end, Hermansen inexplicably flew out and clattered Kilman down the other – almost giving away a fourth in the process- and suddenly, you couldn’t take your eyes off it.

And then – three – three and the roof came off thanks to Max Kilman’s goal from Bowen’s brilliant cross.

Absolutely chaotic scenes in the away end as the incredulous claret and blue army couldn’t believe they’d witnessed a fightback from a team dead and buried at half time.

It could have been four as Trott stretched his fingers to Soucek’s header – agonisingly close as the minutes ticked by. Brilliant second half efforts by Piroe, by Bowen – the man of the match – and excellent impact from Ezra Mayers who might just have found himself a role in Parker’s side.

Nuno’s team in the first half, Parker’s in the  second.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

The 4-2-3-1 system leaves the fullbacks exposed. Our 1st half fullbacks aren’t young or pacy and they needed support that the formation didn’t provide. That said they’ve been our best wide defensive players in other systems. We were too narrow and too focused on playing possession football in the 1st half. That might well be how Parker wants the team to play but we aren’t there yet. Good half time adjustments and excellent 2nd half spirit.

What I was particularly pleased about is that although we snatched a draw in spectacular fashion, there were no player celebrations, just long faces, no smiles. They know even this is not good enough. We are West Ham playing Cardiff in a half empty stadium. We should not struggle, we can not be happy with a draw under any circumstances. We need a winning mentality.

Maybe Jack Moylan is seriously good and we had not done our homework on Cardiff.

Lesson given and learnt then we started playing. Now just need to score three in both halves for the rest of our games and Scotty has done a good job.

How is kante not the first name on the team sheet after Bowen and mavropanos? He’s got everything and I really think the boy will have a distinguished career. Shocking first half, abysmal. Second half could have been more of a cricket score than a comeback. Utterly different halves of football. What I would say is austbo has to start and Solomon needs to look at himself. Not the finished article yet but the little Norwegian wants to make things happen. Anyone know if Alvarez is injured or just exiled?

Because he lopes like a giraffe, has poor control, has little anticipation, and he makes rash challenges. He’s not a number 10 and his game doesn’t mesh with Castellanos. On the positive side he has some pace, energy, potential, and unpredictability. He’s much better coming forward from a deeper defensive midfield role next to Engels. He was good tonight. The last 2 games…not so much.

Solomon has had several poor games in a row. He has a higher ceiling than Austbo but he lacks the work-rate and willingness to defend that Bowen demonstrates.

Thank God he took Taty off, he has been coasting for a while now and Piroe showed his real worth, not wasting possession. always looking to play others in and a shot or two.

Mayers, at last playing at LB!! No problems defending, quick & physical enough to help down the left wing – really bright game.

Bowen, his best game of the season, ran the show, brilliant!

Thought Kilman should have come off at half-time – boy, was I wrong.

Fun seeing Noble and Parker after the match, constantly chatting, already planning, assessing, thinking ahead. Going to enjoy the ups and downs of the season knowing we have some wholehearted WHU stalwarts running the show.

Noticeable that our “strikers” failed to score, yet again ! What, exactly, does Castellanos get paid for ? Don’t get carried away by the second half performance. Just remember the first half & realize that we are a poor team, at the moment. You can’t simply give the opposition a big lead & then expect to be able to overcome them in the end. Typical West Ham performance: but WHY ?

#2032. Rangers handed quadruple injury boost as comeback dates revealed

Daisuke Yokota is closing in on a return as Rangers manage several injury concerns.

The Japanese winger is expected to be back by the end of November as he continues his rehabilitation.

Ross McCrorie is further ahead in his recovery and could return to training next week, around the beginning of the international break.

Providing an update on the pair, Rangers boss Derek McInnes said: “Well, it’s certainly a good carrot for them to aim towards. But Yokota should be back with us by the end of the month.

“Ross McCrorie will be back with us at the beginning of next week, maybe at the start of the international break, doing some training with us. So there's two, there's a wee bit of optimism.”

Cammy Devlin and Lawrence Shankland are also making progress, with both targeting a return to the pitch during the first week of December.

That leaves the pair facing a race against time to be available for the League Cup final.

Lewis Ferguson insists Rangers move 'will happen' in big transfer declaration

45-cap Rangers star left out for Scotland clash as national boss reveals reason

Rangers learn match officials for Saturday night Premiership clash vs St Mirren

McInnes said: “I think Cammy and Lawrence will probably both look to be on pitch the first week of December.

“But there's still a bit to do, still a few hurdles to overcome. But I think if everything goes well for them, then there is an opportunity maybe to be available for that game.

“But I think we just need to let them be for now and see where it is. But the fact it's a cup final, it doesn't do them any harm in terms of pushing them on.”

Badredine Bouanani, meanwhile, has reported some illness as a bug continues to work its way through the Rangers squad.

However, the winger is expected to be fine for the weekend. He is due back in on Thursday and should return to training on Friday ahead of Saturday night’s Premiership clash against St Mirren.

Emmanuel Fernandez is also expected to be available despite picking up an ankle problem in Rangers’ win over Aberdeen at Hampden.

The defender’s ankle was described as “a bit of a mess” in the aftermath of Saturday’s match, but he is due to train on Thursday and is expected to be fit for the trip to Paisley.

Yokota’s progress will provide further encouragement for McInnes, with the winger potentially only a matter of weeks away from his return.

“Listen, we have to come together. If we want to win, it has to be everybody. The fans, us, the press, anybody who supports AC Milan. Let’s come together and all make this possible. Ruben is doing a great job, I made the right decision on Ruben.

#2030. Not travelling: Liverpool hit with fresh injury blow hours before flying to Istanbul

Liverpool have been hit by a fresh injury blow on the eve of their Champions League fixture away to Fenerbahce.

The Reds are due to fly to Istanbul today for their fourth European fixture of the season, in which they’ll come up against a former Anfield idol in Dirk Kuyt, who’s in interim charge of the Turkish Super Lig outfit.

While Andoni Iraola was able to welcome back Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz for the defeat to Arsenal at the weekend, his squad for the game on Wednesday has been lessened by a new absentee.

On Tuesday morning, Liverpool FC confirmed on their official website that Ryan Gravenberch has been ruled out of the match against Fenerbahce due to a heel injury.

The 24-year-old – who was an unused substitute against Arsenal – won’t travel with his teammates to Istanbul and will instead remain at the AXA Training Centre to undergo treatment with the Reds’ medical staff.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The Dutchman’s absence for the trip to Turkiye comes as a setback to Liverpool for what’ll be a true test of character in the hotbed that is the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

The midfielder might’ve had a difficult outing against Chelsea last week, needlessly giving away a penalty in the first half and then fluffing his lines in the shootout later that night, but he’s still a hugely important presence in Iraola’s squad and will be missed tomorrow evening.

The timeline for a return to action is unclear at present, although the head coach will almost certainly be prompted for an update on the 24-year-old when he addresses the media in his pre-match press conference this afternoon.

In the absence of Gravenberch, we could well see Trey Nyoni keeping his starting berth in midfield alongside Alexis Mac Allister, with the duo putting in solid performances on Sunday despite the result against Arsenal.

If that engine room axis is maintained in Istanbul, hopefully the pair can maintain the high standards they’ve shown recently, and fingers crossed for a swift recovery for the Netherlands international as he watches on from Merseyside.

#2029. Kasper Hogh handed Celtic lifeline with slap in the face ahead of five-game gauntlet

Kasper Hogh has been dealt a blow which could yet spark his Celtic redemption arc.

The Danish striker played in all four of his country's games during the extended September and October international break, but has now been left out amid his worrying form for the toiling Premiership champions.

Celtic desperately need something to change with their £11million man and, perhaps, a chance to pause and take stock rather than continuing to operate on the fringes could work in Hogh's favour.

The timing might help him, too. Celtic face Besiktas and Kilmarnock at home before the international break, then return against St Mirren before finishing November with trips to Torreense in the Europa League and Hearts in the Premiership.

Read more: 60 days after my last Celtic appearance, I've returned to first-team training

It's a run which offers Hogh opportunities to rediscover his touch in front of goal. The club-record signing from Bodo/Glimt has scored in just one game for Celtic, albeit a hat-trick against Kilmarnock, and it's hard to dress up an international snub as a positive. In this case, though, it just might be.

A chance to reset, coupled with that potentially favourable run of fixtures, could give Hogh the opportunity to get himself back on track and chase Martin O'Neill's lofty 20-goal target for his much-maligned striker.

Hogh has now gone 14 games without scoring since his hat-trick against Kilmarnock on August 9, drawing blanks against Dundee United twice, LASK twice, St Johnstone, Rangers twice, Ferencvaros, Motherwell, Benfica, Hearts, Celta Vigo, Hibs and Falkirk.

And the big striker has now suffered another setback after being left out of Brian Riemer's Denmark squad for the crunch matches against Portugal and Norway.

#2028. GdS: Why Milan and Inter are expected to bench their most in-form players

Alphadjo Cisse and Carlo Augusto are both expected to start on the bench in tonight’s Derby della Madonnina, despite being among the best players for AC Milan and Inter so far.

For Milan, tonight’s derby is a chance to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture and to decrease the gap in the standings. For Inter, it’s a chance to end the winless run and to truly assert themselves against the Rossoneri, with +10 in sight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In other words, it’s a very important game and the tactical battle is expected to play an important role in the outcome. Team selection is thus top of mind for Ruben Amorim and Cristian Chivu who, however, are looking to bench a couple of their best players: Cisse and Augusto.

Starting with Cisse, as Gazzetta dello Sport highlights, Amorim’s decision is both tactical and psychological. He fears that there will be too much pressure on the youngster’s shoulders, while the plan is also to play with a 4-4-1-1 that can turn into a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 depending on the moment.

In that sense, Amorim believes Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are better suited to playing out wide than Cisse. More specifically, they arre better suited to playing out wide when not in possession, where Inter will push hard.

Playing with attacking-minded midfielders like Moreira and Pulisic, plus a trequartista like Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos (i.e. a 4-2-3-1), would result in an unbalanced team. Behind Ramos there will be Rabiot, who, when not in possession, will act as a central midfielder.

Therefore, Cisse will start on the bench and be used as needed in the second half.

Moving on to Augusto, over the past two months, he has saved Inter on numerous occasions: the assist that started the comeback against Napoli, the goal in Madrid, the turnaround goal against Bologna, and the decisive blow in the Champions League against Shakhtar.

The latest contribution was the own goal he forced against Venezia, which Chivu’s men used to seal a game that could have gone terribly wrong. Yet, in tonight’s derby against Milan, the Brazilian could start on the bench.

The battle with Federico Dimarco will be decided in the final hours, but the reality is that the Italian is still considered the starter on the left. As such, it’s a question of hierarchy, though we will likely see the player come off the bench either way.

#2027. Report: Liverpool increasingly likely to sanction January exit for player in ‘agonising’ situation

One Liverpool player seems increasingly likely to leave Anfield in January as his situation on Merseyside becomes ‘increasingly agonising’.

Having struggled for starts in two seasons under Arne Slot, Federico Chiesa would no doubt have been hoping that a change of head coach might’ve provided the springboard towards an increase in game-time.

Instead, the 29-year-old’s standing at LFC has diminished even further, having played just two minutes under Andoni Iraola so far despite recovering from a back injury almost a month ago.

According to Dean Jones for Flashscore, a January exit from Liverpool for the forward seems ‘increasingly possible’, and a return to his native Italy ‘could provide an attractive solution’ for both player and club.

Lazio, Inter Milan and Roma have been touted as clubs who ‘could explore the possibility’ of bringing Chiesa back to Serie A after he left Juventus for the Reds in 2024, although any such move would depend on what kind of deal the Merseysiders are prepared to consider.

The report adds that the 29-year-old’s situation ‘is becoming increasingly agonising’ as he continues to struggle for game-time at Anfield.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That Chiesa didn’t even make the substitutes’ bench against Arsenal on Sunday despite being fit and available is a damning indictment of where he stands in the pecking order.

The additions of Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola over the summer added further competition for places in the forward line, and the form of Lewis Koumas has seen him leap ahead of the Italian in the queue.

Iraola had six forwards either as starters or substitutes at the weekend, and he still has Hugo Ekitike to return from injury, so Chiesa is effectively our eighth-choice attacker.

His status at Liverpool was summed up a few weeks ago by Roy Keane’s throwaway comment of ‘Is he still there?‘ when the 29-year-old’s name was mentioned on the Stick To Football podcast, and the situation hasn’t gotten any better for our number 14 in the meantime.

Barring a substantial injury crisis in the forward line (heaven forbid), it’s hard to see the Italian getting much of a look-in at Anfield any time soon, and it’s looking increasingly likely that he could be allowed to leave for his homeland in January.

It’d be a shame of his time with the Reds petered out to that extent, but Chiesa would depart as a genuine cult hero among Kopites for what he has contributed over the past two-and-a-bit years.

#2026. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.
